sections.title: Daily Status Check
sections.purpose: Quick health check of all v4 subsystems. Run this daily or after any change.
safety_notes: All commands are read-only — no side effects.
If any check fails, investigate before running further commands.

sections.title: Capability Registry Review
sections.purpose: Review registered external capability adapters and their status.
safety_notes: Registry is the single source of truth for external capability existence.
Never enable a disabled adapter without passing the trial gate first.
Do not add registry entries without Phase 2 compliance checks.

sections.title: Evidence Inspection
sections.purpose: Inspect evidence bundles to verify external adapter outputs are recorded correctly.
safety_notes: All evidence records have truth_source=False — evidence is NOT truth.
Evidence is always TRUST_LOW by default.
Never base kernel decisions on evidence alone.

sections.title: Context Pack Planning
sections.purpose: Plan context packs for codebase analysis without executing external tools.
safety_notes: Context pack planning is dry-run by default — no files are read outside budget.
Use --allow-execute only when you fully trust the target directory.

sections.title: Usage Report Inspection
sections.purpose: Inspect Claude Code usage reports for operational insights.
safety_notes: Usage reports are external evidence, not kernel truth.
Do not use usage data for automated decision-making.

sections.title: Orchestration Dry-Run
sections.purpose: Plan capability adapter orchestration without executing anything.
safety_notes: All orchestration is dry-run only — nothing is executed.
Orchestration plans are PLANS, not truth sources.
ECC profile (ecc_harness_review) is disabled and must stay disabled.

sections.title: Eval / Regression Check
sections.purpose: Run deterministic eval suite and regression matrix to verify v4 integrity.
safety_notes: All evals are deterministic and local — no network, no LLM.
Regression failures that are 'release blocking' must be fixed before merging.
Benefit-complexity REJECT means the change adds too much complexity for too little benefit.

sections.title: Complexity Gate Check
sections.purpose: Verify complexity budget is not exceeded by recent changes.
safety_notes: Complexity gate REJECT blocks all further changes.
REVIEW means the change needs justification before proceeding.
ACCEPT means complexity is within budget for the benefit provided.

sections.title: What NOT to Do
sections.purpose: Operational boundaries that must not be crossed.
safety_notes: DO NOT execute external tools through the kernel boundary.
DO NOT enable blocked providers (OpenHands, AutoGen, Mem0, Graphiti, etc.) without a formal trial.
DO NOT modify v3/kernel/ files — kernel is sealed.
DO NOT modify v3/memory/ runtime behavior.
DO NOT add new truth sources — truth_source must always be False for external data.
DO NOT add LLM/AI imports to kernel modules.
DO NOT install or clone ECC — it is a future external provider, not a dependency.
DO NOT modify registry.json or skill files through automation — use proposal-only skill evolution.

sections.title: How ECC is Treated
sections.purpose: ECC (everything-claude-code) is a FUTURE external harness enhancement provider.
commands: # Status: NOT integrated, NOT cloned, NOT installed
safety_notes: ECC is listed as ecc_harness_review profile — disabled, dry-run only.
ECC capability types: skill, tool, eval, context (4 of 8).
ECC must never be auto-installed, auto-cloned, or auto-executed.
ECC integration requires a formal Phase 12+ trial gate.
SystemKernel must not become an ECC clone or dependency.

sections.title: How to Propose a Real Provider Trial Safely
sections.purpose: Procedure for graduating a blocked provider to trial status.

safety_notes: Never enable a provider without explicit human approval.
All trial proposals are dry-run by default.
Provider enablement requires registry update — do NOT do this automatically.
ECC requires its own formal trial gate before any integration.
